name: ssh
description: Open a secure shell session on a remote host.

flags.description: Remote port
Identity (private key) file
Login user name (alternative to user@host)
Connect through one or more jump hosts
Force a pseudo-terminal (needed for interactive remote commands)
Forward your ssh-agent to the remote host
Set any config option, e.g. -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new
Verbose debugging output

examples.description: Connect as user on the default port 22
Connect on a non-standard port
Use a specific private key
Connect using a Host alias from ~/.ssh/config

notes: Only use -A (agent forwarding) with hosts you trust: root on the remote host can use your agent while you're connected. Prefer -J for hopping through bastions.
When using -i with many keys loaded in the agent, add -o IdentitiesOnly=yes to avoid "Too many authentication failures".

name: ssh -J
description: Connect to a private host through a bastion/jump host.

examples.description: Hop through a bastion to an internal server
Chain multiple jump hosts

examples.command:
Host internal-db
    HostName 10.0.1.20
    User ubuntu
    ProxyJump bastion
examples.description: Equivalent ~/.ssh/config entry using ProxyJump

notes: The connection to the target is end-to-end encrypted through the bastion; your keys never leave your machine (unlike agent forwarding).
ProxyJump/-J requires OpenSSH 7.3+; older setups used ProxyCommand ssh -W %h:%p bastion.

name: ssh host command
description: Run a single command on a remote host without opening an interactive shell.

examples.description: Run a command and print its output locally
Run a command that needs a TTY (e.g. sudo password prompt)
Run a local script on the remote host
Stream a directory to the remote host through a pipe

notes: Quote the remote command so your local shell doesn't expand variables or globs first.

description: Use SSH escape sequences to control a session, e.g. kill a frozen connection.

examples.description: Terminate a hung session (press Enter first, then ~ then .)
List all available escape sequences
List forwarded connections
Show information about the current connection (OpenSSH 10.3+)
Suspend ssh and return to the local shell (resume with fg)

notes: Escape sequences are only recognized right after a newline, so press Enter before typing ~.
In nested SSH sessions, type ~~. to send the escape to the inner session.
~C (command line to add forwards) is disabled by default since OpenSSH 9.2; enable with EnableEscapeCommandline yes.

name: ssh-keygen -t ed25519
description: Generate a new SSH key pair.

flags.description: Key type: ed25519 (default since OpenSSH 9.5), ecdsa, rsa, ed25519-sk/ecdsa-sk (FIDO hardware keys), mldsa44-ed25519 (post-quantum hybrid, OpenSSH 10.6+)
Key size in bits (RSA only in practice: default 3072, 4096 also common; ignored for Ed25519)
Comment, usually an email or machine name
Output file path
New passphrase (use "" for none, e.g. in automation)

examples.description: Generate an Ed25519 key in ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 with a comment
Generate a key with a custom filename
Generate a key backed by a FIDO2 security key (touch required to use it)
Generate an RSA key for legacy systems that don't support Ed25519

notes: Protect keys with a passphrase and use ssh-agent so you only type it once.
Never share the private key (the file without .pub).
DSA keys are no longer supported (removed in OpenSSH 10.0); replace any old id_dsa keys.

name: ssh-keygen -lf
description: Show the fingerprint of a key, or derive the public key from a private key.

examples.description: Show the SHA256 fingerprint of a key
Show the legacy MD5 fingerprint
Regenerate a lost public key from the private key
Show a server's host key fingerprint to verify first connections

name: ssh-keygen -p
description: Add, change or remove the passphrase on an existing private key.

examples.description: Change the passphrase (prompts for old and new)

notes: Changing the passphrase does not change the key itself, so authorized_keys entries keep working.

name: ssh-keygen -Y sign
description: Sign and verify files (or Git commits) with an SSH key instead of GPG.

flags.description: Sign the given files (writes file.sig) or stdin
Verify a signature against an allowed signers file
Signature namespace, e.g. file, email or git (required)
Key file when signing; allowed signers file when verifying
Signer identity to check when verifying
Signature file to verify

examples.description: Sign a file, producing release.tar.gz.sig

examples.command: ssh-keygen -Y verify -f allowed_signers -I user@example.com -n file -s release.tar.gz.sig < release.tar.gz
examples.description: Verify the signature (exit status 0 on success)
Allowed signers file format: identity followed by the public key

examples.command: git config --global gpg.format ssh && git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
examples.description: Use your SSH key to sign Git commits and tags

notes: The namespace used for signing must match the one used for verifying; Git uses the git namespace automatically.

name: ssh-keygen -s
description: Sign user or host keys with an SSH certificate authority (CA) for short-lived, centrally trusted access.

flags.description: CA private key used to sign
Key identity, recorded in server logs
Principals: user names (or host names with -h) the certificate is valid for
Validity interval, e.g. +52w or +1h
Create a host certificate instead of a user certificate
Print the contents of a certificate

examples.description: Create a CA key pair (keep user_ca offline and protected)
Issue an 8-hour certificate, written to ~/.ssh/id_ed25519-cert.pub
Inspect principals and validity of a certificate
sshd_config line that makes the server trust certificates signed by the CA
Sign a host key; clients trust it with a @cert-authority line in known_hosts

notes: ssh automatically uses id_ed25519-cert.pub when it sits next to id_ed25519.
WARNING: anyone holding the CA private key can log in as any principal it trusts; store it offline or in a hardware token.

name: ssh-copy-id
description: Install your public key in a remote host's authorized_keys for passwordless login.

examples.description: Copy your default public key(s) to the server
Copy a specific key to a server on a custom port

examples.command: cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub | ssh user@example.com 'mkdir -p ~/.ssh && chmod 700 ~/.ssh && cat >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys && chmod 600 ~/.ssh/authorized_keys'
examples.description: Manual equivalent when ssh-copy-id isn't available

notes: Requires password (or another working) authentication the first time.
If key login still fails, check permissions: ~/.ssh must be 700 and authorized_keys 600, owned by the user.

name: ssh-agent
description: Start an agent that holds decrypted private keys in memory.

examples.description: Start an agent and export its environment variables in the current shell
Check whether an agent is available
Kill the agent started in this shell

notes: macOS and most Linux desktops start an agent automatically; you usually only need ssh-add.
Since OpenSSH 10.1 the agent socket lives under ~/.ssh/agent/ instead of /tmp; ssh-agent -T restores the old /tmp location.

name: ssh-add
description: Add, list or remove keys in the running ssh-agent.

flags.description: List loaded key fingerprints
List loaded public keys
Remove a specific key
Remove all keys
Lifetime for the key
Load resident keys from a FIDO security key
macOS only: save the passphrase in Keychain (replaces Apple's deprecated -K; upstream -K loads FIDO resident keys)

examples.description: Add a key (prompts for its passphrase once)
List fingerprints of loaded keys
Remove all keys from the agent
macOS: add the key and store its passphrase in the Keychain
Add a key that expires from the agent after one hour

notes: On macOS, also add UseKeychain yes and AddKeysToAgent yes under Host * in ~/.ssh/config so keys load automatically.
"The agent has no identities" from -l means no keys are loaded.

name: ssh -L
description: Local port forwarding: access a remote service through a local port.

examples.description: Reach the server's PostgreSQL at localhost:5433
Reach an internal host via the bastion at localhost:8080
Forward MySQL without opening a shell

notes: Format is -L [bind_address:]local_port:target_host:target_port; target_host is resolved from the remote side.
Ports below 1024 need root locally.

name: ssh -R
description: Remote port forwarding: expose a local service on a port of the remote host.

examples.description: Make your local port 3000 available as port 8080 on the server
Reverse tunnel so you can SSH back into this machine via the relay

notes: By default the remote port binds to loopback only; binding publicly requires GatewayPorts yes in the server's sshd_config.
Exposing local services publicly is a security risk; restrict who can reach the port.

name: ssh -D
description: Dynamic port forwarding: run a local SOCKS proxy through the remote host.

examples.description: Start a SOCKS5 proxy on localhost:1080
Send a request through the proxy with DNS resolved remotely

notes: Configure your browser or tool to use SOCKS5 proxy localhost:1080.

name: ssh -N -f
description: Run a tunnel in the background without a remote shell.

flags.description: Do not execute a remote command (forwarding only)
Go to background after authentication
Fail instead of silently running without the forward

examples.description: Background a tunnel after authentication
Exit with an error if the port can't be forwarded
Stop the background tunnel

notes: For long-lived tunnels add -o ServerAliveInterval=60, or use autossh.

name: ~/.ssh/config
description: Define per-host aliases and options so you can type ssh myserver.

examples.command:
Host myserver
    HostName 203.0.113.10
    User deploy
    Port 2222
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work
    IdentitiesOnly yes
examples.description: Alias with host, user, port and key

examples.command:
Host github.com-work
    HostName github.com
    User git
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_work
examples.description: Use a separate key for a second GitHub account (clone with git@github.com-work:org/repo.git)

examples.command:
Host *
    AddKeysToAgent yes
    UseKeychain yes
    ServerAliveInterval 60
examples.description: Defaults for all hosts (UseKeychain is macOS only)
Print the effective configuration ssh will use for a host

notes: The first matching value wins, so put specific Host blocks above Host *.
The file should be chmod 600.

name: ControlMaster
description: Reuse one SSH connection for multiple sessions (multiplexing) to make repeat connections instant.

examples.description: Enable multiplexing in ~/.ssh/config, keeping the master open 10 minutes after the last session (%C is a short hash of user, host and port)
Check whether a master connection is running
Show details of the master connection (OpenSSH 10.3+; -O channels lists open channels)
Close the master connection

notes: Speeds up tools that open many connections (git, Ansible, scp loops).
If a master hangs after a network change, ssh -O exit or delete the control socket.

name: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
description: Control which public keys may log in to an account, optionally restricting what each key can do.

examples.description: Basic entry: one public key per line
Only accept this key from a given network
Lock a key down to one forced command with no forwarding or PTY
Allow only a tunnel to one port
Key stops working after a date

notes: restrict disables all forwarding, PTY allocation and ~/.ssh/rc; re-enable individual features after it.
The file must not be writable by others (chmod 600, ~/.ssh 700) or sshd ignores it with StrictModes.

name: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
description: Harden the SSH server: disable passwords and root login, and restrict who can connect.

examples.command:
PasswordAuthentication no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
examples.description: Key-only logins and no direct root login
Only allow specific accounts to log in
Relax a setting only for an internal network (Match blocks go at the end)
Many distros Include /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf; put overrides there

examples.command: sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
examples.description: Validate, then apply (service is sshd on RHEL/Fedora)

notes: The first value found for an option wins, so a drop-in in sshd_config.d read before the main file overrides it.
PermitRootLogin defaults to prohibit-password (key-based root login allowed).
WARNING: keep an existing session open and test a new login before closing it, or a mistake can lock you out.

name: scp
description: Copy files between hosts over SSH.

flags.description: Copy directories recursively
Remote port (note: capital P)
Identity file
Enable compression
Use the legacy SCP protocol instead of SFTP

examples.description: Upload a file
Download a file to the current directory
Copy a directory recursively
Use a custom port (capital -P)

notes: Since OpenSSH 9.0, scp uses the SFTP protocol by default; use -O for old servers without SFTP.
For large or repeated syncs, rsync is faster and resumable.
scp -R (remote-to-remote copy run on the origin host) is deprecated since OpenSSH 10.6 and prints a warning; plain remote-to-remote copies already go through the local host.

name: sftp
description: Interactive file transfer session over SSH.

examples.description: Open an SFTP session
Connect on a custom port
Upload a directory (inside sftp)
Download a file (inside sftp)
Resume an interrupted download (inside sftp; reput resumes uploads)
Create nested remote directories (inside sftp, OpenSSH 10.6+)

notes: Inside sftp: ls/cd act on the remote side, lls/lcd on the local side.
Batch mode: sftp -b commands.txt user@example.com.

name: sshfs
description: Mount a remote directory locally over SSH.

examples.description: Mount a remote directory
Auto-reconnect after network drops
Unmount on Linux (fusermount3 -u on newer distros)
Unmount on macOS

notes: Not part of OpenSSH; install the sshfs package. macOS needs macFUSE plus an sshfs build.
The mount point directory must exist and be empty.

name: ssh -vvv
description: Print verbose debug output to diagnose connection and authentication problems.

examples.description: Basic debugging: see which keys are offered and which auth methods succeed
Filter debug output for authentication details
List the public keys ssh would try, in order, and exit (OpenSSH 10.5+)
Test GitHub SSH authentication

notes: Server-side details are in the auth log: journalctl -u ssh (Debian/Ubuntu, sshd on RHEL) or /var/log/auth.log.
OpenSSH 10.1+ warns when the connection does not use a post-quantum key exchange (usually an outdated server). Upgrade the server; WarnWeakCrypto no-pq-kex in ssh_config silences only that warning.

name: known_hosts
description: Manage trusted host keys and fix "REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED" errors.

examples.description: Remove the stored key for a host (after a legitimate rebuild)
Remove the key for a host on a non-standard port
Check whether a host is in known_hosts
Pre-populate a host key (e.g. in CI); verify the fingerprint against the provider's published value

notes: A changed host key can mean a man-in-the-middle attack. Only remove the entry when you know the server was reinstalled or its key rotated.
-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new accepts new hosts automatically but still rejects changed keys; avoid StrictHostKeyChecking=no.

name: sshd
description: Validate and reload the SSH server configuration.

examples.description: Test /etc/ssh/sshd_config for errors
Print the effective server setting for an option
Print the effective config for a specific connection, applying Match blocks
Apply config changes (service is sshd on RHEL/Fedora)

notes: Keep an existing session open while changing sshd_config (e.g. disabling PasswordAuthentication) so a mistake can't lock you out.
Run sshd -t before reloading.
Since OpenSSH 9.8 each connection runs in a separate sshd-session process (sshd-auth handles authentication since 10.0), so process names in ps differ from older releases.
